title: Knowledge, action and the doer, in three kinds

verses.sa: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः । न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥
verses.tr: Whatever action a person begins through body, speech, and mind, right or wrong, has these five causes.
verses.angle: sariravangmanobhih, through body, speech, and mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is about to name the five forces behind every action. Listen for the one word that tells you what a person actually uses to act.

body.text: Whatever action a person begins through body, speech, and mind, right or wrong, has these five causes. The word to hear is sariravangmanobhih, through body, speech, and mind. It shows that a person acts with all three at once, and that every action, whether right or wrong, is driven by the same five causes. Krishna then says that anyone who thinks the pure self alone is the doer has not seen rightly, because the five causes are always present.

verses.sa: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verses.tr: But one who sees only the pure self as the doer, even though these five causes are present, has not seen rightly; such a confused mind does not understand.
verses.angle: Action has many causes; the pure self is not the lone doer.
verses.speaker: Krishna

body.text: But one who sees only the pure self as the doer, even though these five causes are present, has not seen rightly; such a confused mind does not understand. Krishna calls the person who sees the pure self as the sole doer confused, blind to the five causes. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते । हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
verses.tr: One who has no sense of separate self and whose understanding remains unstained does not kill, even by killing all these beings, and is not bound.
verses.angle: Lipyate: the mind that does not stick
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now turns to the person who acts without that false sense of doership, and names the two qualities that keep the mind pure.

body.text: One who has no sense of separate self and whose understanding remains unstained does not kill, even by killing all these beings, and is not bound. Listen to the word lipyate, which means to stick or cling. A mind that does not cling to the act is a mind that is not bound. The next verse names the three things that drive every action and the three parts that make it up.

verses.sa: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना । करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥
verses.tr: Knowledge, the object known, and the knower, these three drive action. Instrument, act, and actor, these three make up the whole of action.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: How does action actually work? Listen to how Krishna breaks it down into its simplest parts before Arjuna can let go of the idea of being the doer.

body.text: Knowledge, the object known, and the knower, these three drive action. Instrument, act, and actor, these three make up the whole of action. Krishna lists the knower, the known, and the knowing as the impulse to act, and the instrument, the act, and the actor as the whole of action. Krishna now shows how each of these three parts is itself threefold, linking them to the three qualities. Listen to that next.

verses.sa: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः । प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥
verses.tr: In the analysis of the three qualities, knowledge, action, and the doer are each said to be threefold. Listen now to these distinctions as they truly are.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains how the three qualities shape the world. Listen for how they divide knowledge, action, and the doer into three kinds each.

body.text: In the analysis of the three qualities, knowledge, action, and the doer are each said to be threefold. Listen now to these distinctions as they truly are. Using the three gunas, Krishna announces that knowledge, action and the doer each come in three kinds. Krishna then defines sattvic knowledge as seeing the one undivided reality in all divided beings.

verses.sa: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
verses.tr: Know that knowledge to be sattvic by which one sees the one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the single word that tells you whether a person sees reality as one or many. Krishna points to the quality of the vision itself.

body.text: Know that knowledge to be sattvic by which one sees the one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided. The pivot is the word avibhakta, undivided, placed right beside vibhakta, divided. The knowledge is sattvic because it sees the one unbroken reality inside every single being. Krishna then turns to the opposite vision, the one that sees many separate beings. Listen to how he names that knowledge.

verses.sa: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् । वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
verses.tr: But know that knowledge as rajasic by which one sees many different beings as separate and distinct in all beings.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described clear vision that sees unity. Now he turns to the restless mind. Listen for how he names the divided view.

body.text: But know that knowledge as rajasic by which one sees many different beings as separate and distinct in all beings. Notice the word 'tu', but. Krishna places this divided seeing against the unity he described in the previous verse, marking it as a lower state of understanding. Krishna then describes the lowest kind of understanding, the dark, that clings to a single body as the whole truth.

verses.sa: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् । अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
verses.tr: But knowledge that clings to one body as if it were the whole, without reason, without truth, and petty, is called dark.
verses.angle: Tamasic knowledge mistakes one body for the whole
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just named rajasic knowledge, which sees many separate beings. Now he names the lowest kind, tamasic knowledge.

body.text: But knowledge that clings to one body as if it were the whole, without reason, without truth, and petty, is called dark. Krishna calls this tamasic knowledge because it clings to one limited thing, a single body or action, and mistakes it for the whole. It lacks clear reason and misses the truth. Krishna then turns to action, describing the sattvic kind that is done without craving or attachment.

verses.sa: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: Action that is guided by duty, free from attachment, and done without craving results is called sattvic.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now asks what makes an action truly sattvic, guiding us to the quality of selfless duty.

body.text: Action that is guided by duty, free from attachment, and done without craving results is called sattvic. The verse says sattvic action is prescribed, free from attachment, and done without craving fruit. It is action performed as duty, stripped of the pull of likes and dislikes. Krishna next describes rajasic action as that driven by desire for pleasure, ego, or great strain.

verses.sa: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
verses.tr: But action done with desire for pleasure, or with ego, or with great strain, is said to be rajasic.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is sorting action into three qualities. This time, he names the restless kind, driven by desire, ego, and strain.

body.text: But action done with desire for pleasure, or with ego, or with great strain, is said to be rajasic. The verse says that action done with ego, or with great strain, is called rajasic. The word sahankarena is the key, because it means with ego, and that ego is what makes an otherwise busy action restless. Next, Krishna names the third kind of action, one done in delusion without regard for the consequences.

verses.sa: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: Action begun in delusion, ignoring its consequences, harm, and one’s own capacity, is called tamasic.
verses.angle: Anupreksham: the refusal to weigh anything
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described passionate action. Now he tells us about the worst kind. Listen for the four things a dark actor refuses to consider.

body.text: Action begun in delusion, ignoring its consequences, harm, and one’s own capacity, is called tamasic. Listen for the word anupreksham, without considering. A tamasic actor looks at the world and simply refuses to weigh the consequence, the loss, the harm, or their own capacity to finish it. Krishna then describes the opposite kind of actor, one who is steady and unchanged by success or failure.

verses.sa: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
verses.tr: The doer who is free from attachment, free from ego, endowed with steadiness and enthusiasm, and unchanged by success or failure is called sattvic.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is now judging the person behind the action, showing Arjuna the ideal doer who works without attachment or ego.

body.text: The doer who is free from attachment, free from ego, endowed with steadiness and enthusiasm, and unchanged by success or failure is called sattvic. The sattvic doer works free of attachment and boasting, with resolve and zeal, unmoved by success or failure. The next verse describes the passionate doer, ruled by craving and chasing results.

verses.sa: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
verses.tr: The doer ruled by craving, chasing results, greedy, violent in nature, impure, and tossed by joy and sorrow is called passionate.
verses.angle: rajasic doer is impure and restless
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the steady doer; now he names the restless middle path.

body.text: The doer ruled by craving, chasing results, greedy, violent in nature, impure, and tossed by joy and sorrow is called passionate. Krishna calls the rajasic doer impure, and that word reveals a restless mind that wants the reward, resents the loss, and cannot rest. Next, Krishna names the doer who is careless, crude, and lazy, the tamasic doer.

verses.sa: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
verses.tr: A careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, lazy, gloomy, and procrastinating doer is called tamasic.
verses.angle: The procrastinating doer is trapped in gloom
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the passionate doer. Now he names the third and lowest type. Listen for the seven marks that define it.

body.text: A careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, lazy, gloomy, and procrastinating doer is called tamasic. This verse lists seven marks, but one stands out: procrastination. The doer is not merely lazy, he is delaying, which traps him in a cycle of gloom and inaction. Krishna now turns to the three qualities that shape how a person understands and acts.

verses.sa: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु । प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥
verses.tr: O Dhananjaya, now hear the threefold distinctions of understanding and steadfastness according to the three qualities, fully and separately explained.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now turns to the inner equipment of the mind, the tools of understanding and steadfastness.

body.text: O Dhananjaya, now hear the threefold distinctions of understanding and steadfastness according to the three qualities, fully and separately explained. Krishna turns to buddhi and dhriti, the mind and resolve, and promises to separate each into its three qualities. Sattvic buddhi is the clarity that knows what binds and what frees.
